packageRules.description: Automerge routine non-major updates after required checks pass.
Immich server and machine learning must always move together.
The Beszel hub and both agent variants share one release train.

The Postgres+vector image is copied verbatim, digest included, from docker/docker-compose.yml at the pinned Immich release's git tag. Its extension versions are coupled to the Immich schema, so it follows an Immich upgrade by hand and never moves on its own.
Bumping Immich also means re-copying the redis and database lines from that release's compose, and updating immich_restore_expected_immich_version plus the pinned preference schema.
Database major versions change on-disk formats that Ansible cannot migrate.

A Seafile series change is not a digest bump. Upgrading requires out-of-band steps no bot can perform: re-downloading upstream's seafile-server.yml for the new series, changing COMPOSE_FILE to match it, and hand-editing seafile.conf and seahub_settings.py inside the volume to drop blocks the new release no longer accepts. The migrations upgrade.py chains are one-way and upstream documents no downgrade, so the pull request is a prompt to do that work, not a finished change. Note what is NOT the reason: upgrade.py does chain every intervening migration script, so intermediate releases need not be stepped through. This covers minor as well as major because Seafile's own terminology inverts Renovate's, and where the line falls was read out of the image rather than assumed: /scripts/upgrade.py decides with is_minor_upgrade, which compares only the first two components of the version. 13.0.27 to 13.0.28 is therefore Seafile-minor and the container runs upgrade/minor-upgrade.sh itself on the next start -- symlink and avatar housekeeping, no schema change and nothing for an operator to do -- which is a Renovate patch, so patches and digest-only refreshes fall through to the routine automerge rule above where they belong. 13.0 to 13.1 is not: it takes upgrade.py's major branch and needs upgrade_13.0_13.1.sh, the same shape as the upgrade_12.0_13.0.sh and upgrade_6.1_6.2.sh the image already ships, and the same manual steps. That is a Renovate minor, which is why the scope stops here rather than at major alone.

The yt-dlp build Pinchflat runs is pinned by version and sha256 together, and a bot cannot compute the checksum. A version bump whose checksum was not updated by hand fails the converge at get_url, so these never automerge: the pull request is a prompt to copy the new SHA2-256SUMS entry, not a finished change.

The Hebrew tessdata model Paperless OCRs with is pinned by tag and sha256 together, and a bot cannot compute the checksum. Worse than the yt-dlp case: tessdata_fast publishes no checksum file, so the new value is produced by downloading heb.traineddata and hashing it. A tag bump whose checksum was not updated by hand fails the converge at get_url, so these never automerge.

customManagers.description: The yt-dlp build Pinchflat runs, pinned in the role defaults because the release image's own copy is frozen behind YouTube and upstream ships no newer release image. Loose versioning is required, not cosmetic: yt-dlp tags like 2026.08.19 are invalid semver because of the zero-padded month, so under the github-releases default this manager matches the line and then silently proposes nothing.

The Hebrew tessdata model Paperless downloads, pinned in the role defaults as a tag inside a raw.githubusercontent.com path. The tag is what makes that path resolve, so github-tags rather than github-releases is the datasource that matches what the URL addresses. The sha256 on the following line is the other half of the pin and is not machine-derivable; see the matching packageRule.
Python tooling pinned in controller-requirements.txt, which the operator guide and production poller install from.
ansible-core pinned by the integration harness.
Requests pinned by the integration harness.
Python image used by the integration sandbox and its cleanup helper. All three files must move together or cleanup pulls a second image.
ansible-core pinned by the Beszel telemetry test, which asserts exact ansible output.

Alpine ruby pinned by the integration harness. The pin uses apk's fuzzy `~` so a distro revision bump cannot drop it out of the index. Alpine's official 3.24-stable APKBUILD is the source of truth for versions available to the runner image.
Alpine curl pinned by the integration harness. Same fuzzy-pin and official branch-tracking reasoning as the ruby manager above.
